title: Medicare GUIDE Program: Dementia Respite Care at Home (20 Visits a Year)
short_title: Medicare may pay for a break from dementia care
description: Caring for someone with dementia at home? The Medicare GUIDE program gives accepted families a dementia care navigator and a 24/7 support line, and families further along can get 20 four-hour respite visits a year, paid by Medicare. Who qualifies (Original Medicare, living at home), what rules it out, and how to get started.

parts.head: Medicare may pay for a break from dementia care
parts.text: Caring for someone with dementia at home? Medicare may pay for you to take a break. It's called the GUIDE program, and most families who qualify have never heard of it. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's how it works.

parts.head: A Medicare program for dementia at home
parts.sub: A care navigator and a 24/7 support line
parts.text: GUIDE is a Medicare program for people living with dementia at home. Every family that's accepted gets a dementia care navigator, and a support line that's open twenty-four seven.

parts.head: A dementia care navigator
parts.sub: A monthly call with someone who has seen this before
parts.text: The care navigator calls you every month. They help you understand what the next stage looks like, which paperwork matters, and where to find help. It's someone to talk to who has seen this before.

parts.head: A 24/7 support line
parts.text: And the support line is there at two in the morning, when she won't settle, and nobody prepared you for what's happening. It's a clinical line that can talk you through it.

parts.head: 20 respite visits a year
parts.sub: 4 hours each. Medicare pays us, not you.
parts.text: For families further along, GUIDE also pays for respite: twenty visits a year, four hours each. A trained caregiver from Caring Companions stays with your loved one, and Medicare pays us, not you.

parts.head: A break is not giving up
parts.sub: Your own doctor, a wedding, or just sleep
parts.text: Respite isn't a luxury, and it isn't giving up. It's the afternoon you get to see your own doctor, go to a family wedding, or just sleep. Families who take regular breaks often keep someone at home much longer.

parts.head: Respite hours depend on the stage
parts.sub: Medicare decides. Early on, you may qualify later.
parts.text: Not every family gets the respite hours right away. Medicare decides, based on how far the dementia has progressed, and how much strain the caregiver is under. If it's early on, you may start with the navigator and support line, and qualify for respite later.

parts.head: Original Medicare, living at home
parts.sub: Not Medicare Advantage. Not assisted living or memory care.
parts.text: Two things decide most of it. First, the kind of Medicare. Traditional, or Original, Medicare works. A Medicare Advantage plan, like Humana or Aetna, doesn't. Second, where they live. At home, alone or with family, is fine. As of June 2026, assisted living and memory care don't qualify, and neither does a nursing home.

parts.head: Hospice and PACE rule it out
parts.sub: Palliative care, Medicaid or VA benefits are fine
parts.text: Medicare hospice and PACE also rule it out. But palliative care is fine, and having Medicaid or VA benefits too is fine.

parts.head: Talk, assessment, approval
parts.sub: Plan on 2 to 3 weeks. Need help sooner? Tell us.
parts.text: Here's how it goes. First, we talk, free, in your home or on the phone. Then we come out and do the assessment with you and your loved one. Plan on two to three weeks for approval. If you need help sooner, tell us, and we'll do our best to start right away.

parts.head: Use the hours through the year
parts.sub: They reset July 1 and don't roll over
parts.text: One tip. The respite hours reset every July first, and unused hours don't roll over. So use them steadily through the year, instead of saving them for a rainy day.
Check if your family qualifies at mo-care.com slash medicare guide, or call us at (417) 234-8494. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
